newsitem.title: USA: Mexico growth insufficient to reduce poverty - IMF.
newsitem.headline: Mexico growth insufficient to reduce poverty - IMF.

text.p: Mexico's economic program is successfully reducing inflation but it has yet to generate enough growth to reduce poverty, International Monetary Fund managing director Michel Camdessus said Thursday.
The Mexican government must also press ahead with the banking sector restructuring program it launched in the wake of the December 1994 peso crisis, he added.

"Our program with Mexico is functioning very well, in terms of reducing inflation inflation and (rekindling) growth, but growth of, say, five percent is still insufficient. More needs to be done," Camdessus said at a news conference.
Mexico posted a 5.1 percent increase in its gross domestic product last year, after suffering a 6.2 percent contraction in 1995 due to its financial crisis.
The IMF's latest projections tip Mexico's GDP to grow by about 4.5 percent in 1997.
Inflation is expected to drop this year to nearly half of last year's 34.1 percent.
Camdessus, who spoke in Spanish, said Mexico and many other Latin American countries would have to turn to a second generation of structural reforms in order to free up their economic potential.

"It is true that Latin America is not growing enough to reduce poverty in a decisive way. It may, it can, and should grow more, but this does not mean anything other than effort, continuous effort," he said.
Nearly one in three Latin Americans are poor, surviving on incomes of less than two dollars a day.
Camdessus acknowledged that the region has been working to improve its macroeconomic base and resume growth, but he noted that there were still other obstacles to reducing poverty.
Latin American nations still face tremendous problems of "governance", Camdessus said, recurring to a term used by multilateral agencies to describe poor public sector management and corruption.

"If we are to be sincere in our desire to reduce poverty, then we must accelerate privatization to make the economy more efficient, we must accept competition, we have to change the role of the state for it to do better what it alone can do, they have to combat corruption and make institutions credible again, put more effort in education and social programs," he said.
